label: Audacity recording and editing adapter
summary: Use Audacity for person-operated recording, waveform editing, and audition while exchanging lossless files through EPRS and keeping scripting opt-in.

handoffs.label: Record a performance and preserve it in EPRS
handoffs.intent: Capture guitar, family voices, chimes, spoken beat ideas, room sound, or another performance without processing the only copy.
inputs: A named performer or source, microphone/setup note, intended role, and consent context
An explicit project sample rate and available recording bit depth
outputs: A lossless WAV, AIFF, or FLAC export of each preserved take
A recording-session record linking take, setup, performer, consent, rights, and notes
steps: Set the intended device, channels, and project sample rate before recording and make a short level test.
Record without automatic normalization, noise reduction, compression, tuning, or tempo correction.
Export each irreplaceable take losslessly, ingest it through EPRS, and retain the native Audacity project when future edits may matter.
verification: Open or probe the exported take and confirm duration, channels, sample rate, bit depth, and absence of truncation or clipping.
Confirm the exported checksum remains unchanged after raw intake and that every participant/setup relationship is recorded.

handoffs.label: Continue an EPRS arrangement in Audacity
handoffs.intent: Import common-start lossless stems, make explicitly documented edits, and return one lossless bounce for ordinary review.
inputs: A verified EPRS DAW-neutral interchange package
Its import instructions, common time-zero origin, and declared stereo stem balances
outputs: A lossless WAV or FLAC bounce beginning at the declared common origin
An eprs.daw-return/v1 declaration of tool/version, operator, edits, settings, unknowns, rights, and added sources
steps: Import every stem at time zero and do not add automatic normalization, warping, fades, polarity changes, or pan.
Make only the intended audible changes and preserve the editable Audacity project separately.
Export one lossless return without overwriting the interchange package, then capture it with eprs interchange return.
verification: Confirm the bounce start, duration, channel layout, sample rate, and lossless encoding.
Record a complete mix-review listen before any returned bounce can reach mastering.

preserve: Every original recording export and the native Audacity project when it contains unique editable work
Human timing, tuning, room sound, breath, dynamics, noise, and silence unless a declared edit intentionally changes them
avoid: Overwriting raw takes, flattening the only editable session, or enabling macros and mod-script-pipe without explicit user choice
Automatic effects, resampling, dither, normalization, tempo matching, or destructive waveform edits that are absent from the handoff record
